field_contract.id: Stable unique identifier. Prefix equals class.
field_contract.statement: One normative, independently verifiable obligation in consistent imperative form.
field_contract.class: FR | BR | DATA | SEC | PRIV | NFR | AUDIT | PILOT | OPS
field_contract.acceptance_state: ACCEPTED (obligation confirmed by canonical discovery) | PROVISIONAL (canonical working direction whose wording or rule may still change) | CONDITIONAL (obligation exists only if a stakeholder decision promotes it)
field_contract.readiness_milestone: PILOT | WITHOUT_JAIME | PUBLIC_LAUNCH — the earliest milestone by which the obligation must hold.
field_contract.status: BASELINED | BLOCKED_BY_VALIDATION. BLOCKED_BY_VALIDATION if and only if at least one validation_link has effect BLOCK.
field_contract.rationale: Why this obligation is necessary for an accepted MVP objective, business rule, safety, compliance, or governed pilot activity.
field_contract.business_source: Canonical discovery section identifiers supporting the complete statement.
field_contract.verification_method: TEST | SECURITY_TEST | INSPECTION | ANALYSIS | DEMONSTRATION | PILOT_EVIDENCE | BUSINESS_REVIEW
field_contract.validation_links: Ordered [effect, gate] pairs. BLOCK means the candidate obligation is recorded but cannot be accepted as final or made implementation-ready until the gate resolves; CALIBRATE defers a value; VALIDATE defers wording, procedure, evidence, or stakeholder confirmation.
field_contract.dependencies: Requirement identifiers this obligation depends on.
field_contract.notes: Non-normative context. Never carries an obligation.
field_contract.block_justifications: Required if and only if status is BLOCKED_BY_VALIDATION. Ordered array with exactly one object per gate linked with effect BLOCK, in the same order as those links. Each object carries reason_code, gate, canonical_open_question, and explanation. See block_justifications_contract.
field_contract.supersedes: Optional. Requirement identifiers whose obligation this record replaces.

block_justifications_contract.purpose: A gate being unresolved is not by itself a reason to block. Every blocked record must name, for every gate it blocks on, which kind of unresolvedness it faces, and that kind must be one in which the obligation cannot yet be accepted as final. The vocabulary deliberately contains no code meaning that only wording, procedure, ownership, or evidence is outstanding, because those are exactly the cases the baseline represents as VALIDATE or CALIBRATE on a BASELINED record. The validator enforces every rule below.
block_justifications_contract.coverage: The set of gates named in block_justifications equals exactly the set of gates linked with effect BLOCK: each such gate is justified exactly once, no justification names a gate that is not so linked, and duplicates on either side are rejected. This is a set equality rather than a membership test, because a membership test would allow a further BLOCK link to be attached to an already blocked record while an unrelated existing justification kept the record valid. That is the unjustified over-blocking this contract exists to make unrepresentable.

reason_code.OBLIGATION_NOT_YET_ACCEPTED: Canonical discovery records the obligation as a working direction, a provisional rule, or a conditional possibility rather than an accepted rule. Whether Dopis imposes it at all is undecided. Requires acceptance_state PROVISIONAL or CONDITIONAL.
reason_code.SUBJECT_MATTER_NOT_YET_SELECTABLE: The obligation refers to a set, register, or matrix that does not yet exist in any form, so no candidate instance of the obligation can be selected. Distinct from a value that is merely unapproved, which is CALIBRATE.
reason_code.AUTHORISATION_NOT_YET_CONFERRED: The record is a milestone entry condition whose whole subject is an authorisation that no stakeholder has granted. Requires a prohibition statement beginning with 'Do not'.

block_justifications_contract.gate: The gate this justification accounts for. Must be one of the gates this record links with effect BLOCK, and each such gate must appear exactly once across the array.
block_justifications_contract.canonical_open_question: Must match an entry in that gate's open_questions verbatim, so that a blocking concern is always a registered open question rather than an unstated one.
block_justifications_contract.acceptance_rule: An ACCEPTED record may use only SUBJECT_MATTER_NOT_YET_SELECTABLE or AUTHORISATION_NOT_YET_CONFERRED. It may never claim its own obligation is undecided.
block_justifications_contract.milestone_note: An unresolved gate can still block a milestone globally through the milestone entry-condition records PILOT-004, OPS-DELEGATION-001, and BR-LAUNCH-001, without every dependent obligation being marked blocked.

requirements.statement: Allow a customer to browse the currently published menu without creating an account.
requirements.rationale: Guest browsing is the entry point of the stated MVP objective to move telephone orders to the web.

requirements.statement: Allow a customer to submit a pickup order without creating an account.
requirements.rationale: Guest checkout is an explicitly confirmed MVP objective.

requirements.statement: Collect customer name and telephone number as the only mandatory customer data for a web or telephone order.
requirements.rationale: Data minimisation on the two channels where canonical discovery accepts both fields: section 2.1 states guest checkout requires a name and telephone number, and a telephone order supplies the number by the nature of the channel.
requirements.notes: Scoped deliberately to the web and telephone channels. The in-person channel is carried by DATA-ORDER-003, which is not accepted, and the cross-channel minimisation ceiling is carried by BR-ORDER-013. This record decides nothing about in-person orders.

requirements.statement: Collect no mandatory customer data beyond customer name and telephone number on any order channel.
requirements.rationale: Data minimisation must bind every channel, including the one whose telephone-number rule is still open, so that an unresolved question can never be resolved by collecting more.
requirements.notes: States the ceiling, not the floor. DATA-ORDER-001 states the accepted floor for web and telephone orders; DATA-ORDER-003 records the undecided in-person floor. This ceiling holds whichever way DATA-ORDER-003 resolves.

requirements.statement: Require a telephone number for every in-person order.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery records collecting a telephone number for in-person orders as a working direction so operational incidents can be communicated by SMS, while section 14 names excessive in-person collection as a risk. Both readings must be preserved until Jaime decides.
requirements.notes: Recorded as a candidate obligation only. Canonical section 7.4A states that requiring a telephone number for every in-person order remains a working decision pending Jaime's validation of operational burden and privacy necessity, so this baseline does not accept it. BR-ORDER-013 keeps minimisation binding meanwhile.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: whether every in-person order genuinely requires a telephone number
block_justifications.explanation: Canonical section 7.4A records this as a working decision pending Jaime's validation of operational burden and privacy necessity. What is undecided is whether Dopis imposes the obligation at all, not how it is worded.

requirements.statement: Accept pickup orders only; do not accept delivery orders or table reservations.
requirements.rationale: Preserves the explicit first-MVP scope exclusion so no later requirement reintroduces delivery.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-DELIVERY-RESERVATION.

requirements.statement: Accept same-day orders only at initial launch.
requirements.rationale: Preserves the explicit exclusion of a multi-day advance-order horizon, which is recorded as a future capability.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-ADVANCE-ORDERS. The advance horizon is configurable in the data model but remains set to same-day for the first MVP.

requirements.statement: Offer an earliest-available pickup opportunity and feasible scheduled pickup opportunities calculated from the final basket, current stock, operating hours, blocked windows, and remaining capacity.
requirements.rationale: The hybrid scheduling flow is the accepted mechanism that prevents both premature time selection and accepting orders with no feasible pickup time.
requirements.notes: The obligation to compute feasible opportunities is accepted. Only the point values and lead time are calibratable, so this is no longer blocked.

requirements.statement: Return the nearest feasible alternative pickup opportunities instead of creating a confirmed order when final revalidation fails.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery explicitly rejects silently accepting an order and rejecting it later; the customer must see alternatives before final confirmation.

requirements.statement: Confirm an order only after final revalidation of ordering mode, service hours, pickup-window feasibility, remaining capacity, product and modifier availability, and applicable stock.
requirements.rationale: Prevents confirming an order the kitchen cannot fulfil; this is the core admission invariant of automatic mode.

requirements.statement: Commit pickup-window capacity and sellable stock transactionally so that simultaneous checkouts cannot overbook the same pickup window or oversell the same unit.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery states capacity commitment must be transactionally safe. Without this invariant the accepted-order guarantees in BR-ORDER-004 and BR-CAPACITY-001 can be violated under concurrency.
requirements.notes: States the required outcome, not a locking strategy. The mechanism is an architecture decision.

requirements.statement: Create a configurable provisional capacity and sellable-stock hold when checkout begins, and release it on expiry or abandonment.
requirements.rationale: The provisional hold is the accepted mechanism that stops a customer completing checkout against capacity or stock that another customer has already taken.
requirements.notes: The initial working hold duration is five minutes; the value is registered in the operational threshold register.

requirements.statement: Allow a cart holding a valid provisional hold to complete submission during an ordering pause, and prevent submission of any cart without a valid hold.
requirements.rationale: Protects a customer already in checkout when staff pause ordering, without letting a stale cart bypass the pause.

requirements.statement: In manual-review mode, allow authorised staff to accept the requested pickup time, reject the order, or propose a feasible alternative pickup time.
requirements.rationale: Manual review is the accepted default operating mode for the pilot and requires these three staff outcomes.

requirements.statement: Allow a customer using private tracking to accept or decline a staff-proposed alternative pickup time within the configured response window, committing the reserved capacity atomically on acceptance.
requirements.rationale: The alternative-slot response is one of only two customer actions the tracking page permits, and it is required to close the manual-review loop.
requirements.notes: The initial working response window is ten minutes. Only the value is calibratable, so this obligation is baselined.

requirements.statement: On expiry of an unanswered alternative-slot proposal, release the reserved capacity and stock, reject the order automatically, and send an outcome SMS.
requirements.rationale: Without a defined expiry outcome, held capacity is never released and the customer receives no resolution.
requirements.notes: How staff should handle an expired proposal when direct customer contact has already occurred remains an open question under JV-DELAYS.

requirements.statement: Allow authorised staff to cancel an order and record the applicable reason.
requirements.rationale: Staff cancellation is the only cancellation path in the first MVP and must be attributable.
requirements.notes: Exact cancellation reason codes and customer communication remain open under JV-DELAYS.

requirements.statement: Do not provide general customer self-service cancellation.
requirements.rationale: Preserves an explicit first-MVP exclusion that a tracking-page requirement could otherwise reintroduce.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-SELF-CANCEL.

requirements.statement: Release reserved stock and unused future pickup-window capacity when an order is cancelled before preparation begins, and release only unused future capacity once preparation has begun.
requirements.rationale: Defines the cancellation side effects so capacity is not permanently lost and consumed stock is not falsely restored.

requirements.statement: Preserve the confirmed price, product commitment, and capacity admission of an accepted order despite later catalog or capacity changes.
requirements.rationale: Accepted-order stability is an explicit canonical invariant and a named risk; without it confirmed customer commitments become unstable.

requirements.statement: Route an accepted order that can no longer be fulfilled as confirmed to the Requires attention queue without silently changing or cancelling it.
requirements.rationale: Complements BR-ORDER-004: the order must surface to staff rather than being mutated or dropped.
requirements.notes: Requires attention is the canonical queue name used throughout this baseline.

requirements.statement: Allow authorised staff to enter telephone and in-person orders through the same order domain, status lifecycle, and kitchen queue used by web orders.
requirements.rationale: Channel parity is stated as a firm canonical rule, and shared kitchen capacity depends on every channel entering the same domain.
requirements.notes: Channel parity itself is accepted. Only order-entry ownership and in-person telephone necessity remain open under JV-MANUAL-CHANNELS.

requirements.statement: Optimise telephone order entry for staff speed while still requiring explicit product, modifier, pickup time, customer name, and telephone data.
requirements.rationale: Telephone entry happens during live service; an unusable flow would push staff back to paper and defeat the channel-parity invariant.
requirements.notes: Acceptable entry speed is demonstrated during the operational rehearsal rather than fixed as a numeric target. The mandatory fields named here are the accepted telephone-channel fields of DATA-ORDER-001.

requirements.statement: Record each order origin as WEB, PHONE, or IN_PERSON.
requirements.rationale: Channel origin is required for the pre-pilot baseline, the weekly report, and the call-reduction outcome measure.

requirements.statement: Give telephone and in-person orders the next feasible pickup opportunity without displacing already confirmed orders.
requirements.rationale: Prevents manual channels from silently overriding commitments already made to web customers.

requirements.statement: Allow authorised staff to switch online ordering among automatic acceptance, manual review, and paused modes.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery requires staff to switch to manual confirmation and to pause online ordering when operational conditions demand it.
requirements.notes: Mode names are taken from canonical discovery section 3.2.

requirements.statement: Allow a customer using private tracking to reject an important revised pickup estimate within the configured response window.
requirements.rationale: The delay rejection is the second and last customer action the tracking page permits, and it is required so a customer is not bound to an estimate they cannot meet.
requirements.notes: What counts as an important revised estimate is deliberately deferred to JV-DELAYS rather than invented here.

requirements.statement: Treat silence as non-acceptance of an important revised pickup estimate, routing the order to manual review, and place an explicit rejection in the Requires attention queue.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery states explicitly that silence does not count as acceptance; the default must not favour Dopis.

requirements.statement: Route an order to manual review when the initial tracking SMS cannot be delivered, rather than rejecting it automatically.
requirements.rationale: A messaging failure is a Dopis-side fault; automatic rejection would penalise the customer for it and lose an accepted order.
requirements.notes: SMS retry behaviour remains an open item under JV-DELAYS.

requirements.statement: Allow staff to mark an order NO_SHOW only manually, after the confirmed pickup window has ended, the configurable grace period has elapsed, and a customer contact attempt has been made.
requirements.rationale: Prevents an automatic no-show penalty and preserves the canonical non-collection procedure, which is otherwise unrepresented in the baseline.
requirements.notes: The initial working grace period is 30 minutes and belongs in the operational threshold register.

requirements.statement: Allow an authorised extension of the non-collection grace period within a configurable maximum.
requirements.rationale: Gives staff a bounded alternative to marking a delayed but reachable customer as a no-show.

requirements.statement: Record an explicit customer cancellation and the operational loss, rather than a no-show, when the customer states they will not collect an already prepared order.
requirements.rationale: Distinguishes a communicated cancellation from an unexplained no-show so customer incident history stays accurate and fair.

requirements.statement: Allow a person other than the ordering customer to collect an order by identifying it with the customer name and order number.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery accepts third-party collection; without it staff have no defined handover path for a common real case.
requirements.notes: Interacts with SEC-CUSTOMER-001, which governs disclosure over the telephone rather than at the counter.

requirements.statement: Make web, telephone, and in-person orders consume the same kitchen capacity, stock, and pickup-window commitments.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: treating a web pause as spare manual-channel capacity would overload the same kitchen.

requirements.statement: Do not allow pausing one ordering channel to release capacity or stock limits for another channel.
requirements.rationale: States the channel-pause invariant explicitly so a pause requirement cannot be read as freeing shared limits.

requirements.statement: Calculate order production load as the integer sum of configurable production points for products and eligible modifiers.
requirements.rationale: Weighted production points are required from the first operational version so a simple and a complex pizza do not consume equal capacity.
requirements.notes: Point values are technical configuration calibrated with Jaime; the weighting model itself is accepted.

requirements.statement: Evaluate order admission against configurable per-window capacity, weekday templates, and date-specific exceptions.
requirements.rationale: Admission control against real pickup-window capacity is the mechanism that keeps pickup promises achievable.
requirements.notes: Initial pickup-window duration is 15 minutes and is a calibratable value.

requirements.statement: Advance the earliest-available pickup estimate when nearer pickup windows are full.
requirements.rationale: Without this the earliest-available offer would advertise times the kitchen has already committed.

requirements.statement: Route an order to manual review when it exceeds the configured large-order percentage of one pickup window's capacity, even if nominal capacity remains.
requirements.rationale: Protects against a single large order consuming a window that the raw capacity calculation would still permit.
requirements.notes: The initial percentage requires validation with real kitchen observation and belongs in the threshold register.

requirements.statement: Route an order whose production load cannot be accommodated within a single pickup window to manual review, and do not distribute it automatically across consecutive windows.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery defers automatic multi-window distribution until a validated production-planning rule exists.

requirements.statement: Allow authorised staff to block and reopen individual pickup windows.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery requires staff to be able to block pickup slots; a blocked window must accept no new orders.

requirements.statement: Allow the responsible person to apply a temporary preparation delay and a temporary capacity reduction limited to the current service.
requirements.rationale: Gives the shift a bounded way to absorb real kitchen pressure without changing permanent policy.

requirements.statement: Reserve permanent changes to normal capacity and operating hours to Jaime, limiting the delegated responsible person to temporary current-service adjustments.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a temporary service adjustment must not silently become permanent policy.

requirements.statement: Record actor, timestamp, affected order, and explicitly acknowledged operational risk for every exceptional capacity override.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an unmeasured override becomes routine and makes pickup promises unreliable.
requirements.notes: When an operator may override calculated capacity remains an open question under JV-SHIFT-AUTHORITY; the auditability obligation is accepted now.

requirements.statement: Configure premises hours, online pizza-ordering start, earliest pickup, latest pickup, minimum lead time, day-specific schedules, and date-specific exceptions as separate values.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery states these are distinct concepts; collapsing them would make the final submission time wrong and block date exceptions.
requirements.notes: Separability is the single obligation here. The concrete weekly baseline values are confirmed in section 13.4.

requirements.statement: Derive the final order-submission opportunity dynamically from latest permitted pickup, minimum lead time, basket workload, remaining capacity, and temporary delays.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery explicitly rejects assuming the cutoff equals the premises closing time.

requirements.statement: Support date-specific closure, exceptional opening, special hours, and special capacity overrides on top of the weekly default schedule.
requirements.rationale: Real service has holidays and exceptional openings; without overrides staff would have to edit the permanent schedule.

requirements.statement: Provide authenticated staff access to the operational kitchen queue and prevent public access to it.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a panel reachable without real backend authorisation exposes and allows manipulation of orders.
requirements.notes: Authentication must be enforced in the backend, not only by a frontend route guard.

requirements.statement: Allow authorised staff to progress orders through the approved status lifecycle while preventing duplicate or invalid transitions.
requirements.rationale: Duplicate or invalid transitions corrupt order state and the audit history the pilot depends on.

requirements.statement: Require staff to select Start preparation to begin preparation formally, and permit and record an earlier start.
requirements.rationale: Start preparation is the event that separates releasable stock from consumed stock; it must be explicit rather than inferred.

requirements.statement: Keep a newly received order visibly highlighted until staff explicitly acknowledge it.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an inaudible alert in a noisy kitchen leaves an order unseen; persistent highlight is the fallback.

requirements.statement: Produce an audible alert for a newly received order that is perceptible under the real music level, tablet position, and kitchen noise.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery records that music makes a standard tablet alert difficult to hear, so audibility must be demonstrated on real equipment.
requirements.notes: Which tablet, browser, placement, and sound level will be used remains open under JV-PILOT. The audibility obligation is accepted and is verified by demonstration on the real device.

requirements.statement: Repeat the alert for an order that remains unacknowledged.
requirements.rationale: A single missed alert must not be the only protection for an accepted order.
requirements.notes: The repeat interval is a calibratable operational threshold.

requirements.statement: Pause automatic acceptance after an order remains unacknowledged beyond the configured timeout, and require explicit staff review and a Resume action before automatic acceptance restarts.
requirements.rationale: Prevents the system from continuing to accept orders into an unattended kitchen.
requirements.notes: The timeout before an unacknowledged order pauses automatic acceptance is a calibratable threshold.

requirements.statement: Pause new online orders after the panel has been disconnected beyond the configured interval, and require explicit staff review and a Resume action before ordering restarts.
requirements.rationale: A disconnected panel cannot receive orders; continuing to accept them would silently strand accepted orders.
requirements.notes: The initial working interval is three minutes and belongs in the operational threshold register.

requirements.statement: Display the panel connection status and identify retained data as stale while disconnected.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: staff acting on stale information believe they are seeing current orders.

requirements.statement: Prevent state-changing actions while the panel is disconnected.
requirements.rationale: Separately verifiable invariant: showing staleness is not sufficient if a stale write can still be committed.
requirements.notes: Split from the former combined connection-status requirement so the write barrier can be verified independently.

requirements.statement: Recover the panel operational view after a browser refresh and provide a manual refresh fallback when live updates fail.
requirements.rationale: Browser logout and refresh are listed canonical failure modes that must not lose the operational view.
requirements.notes: Live-update transport choice is an architecture decision, not a requirement.

requirements.statement: Maintain a documented operational fallback procedure covering internet or Wi-Fi failure, server failure, tablet battery loss, browser logout, and a missed audible notification.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery states the business needs a documented fallback because no printer is in scope.
requirements.notes: The simultaneous tablet, mobile, network, and backend failure procedure remains an open item under JV-PILOT.

requirements.statement: Provide a mobile backup that can view orders, change operational states, and apply urgent availability changes.
requirements.rationale: The mobile backup is the accepted operational fallback for the tablet in the first MVP.

requirements.statement: Prevent the mobile backup from editing prices, commercial content, access permissions, or exposing full administration.
requirements.rationale: A personal mobile device is a weaker trust boundary than the premises tablet; sensitive administration must not follow it.
requirements.notes: Exact mobile-backup permission limits are confirmed under JV-ACCESS; the restriction itself is accepted.

requirements.statement: Require a completed readiness checklist, a recorded responsible person, and an explicit Open orders action before online ordering begins.
requirements.rationale: Opening must be a deliberate act with an accountable person, not a consequence of the clock reaching service time.

requirements.statement: Cover kitchen readiness, shift capacity, countable drinks and desserts, sold-out products, and the configured critical ingredient and option list in the pre-opening checklist.
requirements.rationale: Defines the checklist content so the Open orders gate is a real readiness check rather than a button.
requirements.notes: Which ingredients and options belong to the critical list is confirmed under JV-STOCK.

requirements.statement: Provide large touch targets, high-contrast order states, and complete operation without any hover-dependent action or information.
requirements.rationale: The panel runs on a touch tablet during live service, where hover does not exist and low contrast is unreadable.

requirements.statement: Order operational queues by the calculated recommended preparation time rather than by submission time.
requirements.rationale: Submission order does not reflect kitchen urgency once scheduled orders exist; ordering by preparation time is what prevents late fulfilment.

requirements.statement: Raise the prominence of a delayed order and display its elapsed delay without requiring hover.
requirements.rationale: A delayed order must be visible at a glance for the reliability criterion to hold during peak service.

requirements.statement: Distinguish the Requires attention, active preparation, Ready for pickup, Scheduled, and shift-history queues.
requirements.rationale: These are the canonical operational queues that other requirements route orders into; without them routing obligations have no destination.
requirements.notes: Requires attention is the canonical term for the exception queue across this baseline.

requirements.statement: Keep cancelled orders and unresolved incidents visible until staff select Incident reviewed.
requirements.rationale: Prevents an unresolved incident from disappearing from the shift before anyone has acted on it.

requirements.statement: Enter a scheduled order into the active queue according to calculated workload and available capacity, warning first at its recommended preparation-start time.
requirements.rationale: A scheduled order that appears only at its pickup time cannot be prepared on time.

requirements.statement: Give customer name and pickup time greater visual prominence than the public order identifier in operational views.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery states name and pickup time are operationally more important than the public code.

requirements.statement: Remove handed-over orders from the primary operational view while keeping them available in shift history.
requirements.rationale: Keeps the live queue readable during peak service without losing the shift record.

requirements.statement: Make all order channels reserve and consume from the same stock records.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: telephone or in-person orders bypassing shared stock cause overbooking and stock discrepancies.

requirements.statement: Support an opening count for directly countable products and treat the recorded quantity as a strict online-sales ceiling.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery sets initial inventory scope as availability plus unit stock for countable products, with the opening count as a hard ceiling.
requirements.notes: Which products require counts and who performs them is confirmed under JV-STOCK; the ceiling obligation is accepted.

requirements.statement: Reserve applicable stock during checkout or manual review, commit it on confirmation, and release it on expiry, abandonment, or cancellation before preparation.
requirements.rationale: Reserve-commit-release is the accepted mechanism preventing two customers from buying the same physical unit.
requirements.notes: Hold durations are calibratable values in the operational threshold register.

requirements.statement: Require the customer to remove or replace an item whose stock reaches zero before a reservation was created, before checkout can continue.
requirements.rationale: Defines the customer-side outcome when stock runs out mid-session, which otherwise leaves the basket in an unresolvable state.

requirements.statement: Route an order to the Requires attention queue when a reserved unit is found not to exist physically, and resolve it by an allowed alternative or manual cancellation rather than automatic cancellation.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a valid reservation keeps priority while physical stock exists, and a discovered shortage must not silently cancel a customer's accepted order.

requirements.statement: Allow authorised staff to record replenishment and stock corrections with operator, timestamp, and a configured reason.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery requires countable stock adjustments to record the operator and a simple reason so discrepancies can be explained.
requirements.notes: Initial reason codes are unregistered sale, breakage or waste, internal consumption, incorrect count, and replenishment. Which reasons match real staff practice is confirmed under JV-STOCK.

requirements.statement: Allow any authorised staff member to mark a product, critical ingredient, or option unavailable immediately.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery makes disablement deliberately fast and broadly available so an unfulfillable item stops selling at once.

requirements.statement: Restrict reactivation of pizzas, critical ingredients, and modifier options to Jaime or the responsible shift lead, while permitting drinks and desserts to return to sale once a replenishment is recorded.
requirements.rationale: The asymmetry is intentional: unauthorised reactivation exposes items that cannot actually be fulfilled.

requirements.statement: Do not substitute an unavailable item automatically and do not return an item to sale solely from an estimated replenishment time.
requirements.rationale: Preserves two explicit canonical exclusions; either would cause a customer to order something Dopis cannot supply.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-AUTOMATIC-SUBSTITUTION.

requirements.statement: Keep a sold-out product visible and non-orderable, optionally displaying an estimated return time as informational only.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery keeps sold-out items visible for commercial reasons while forbidding an estimated time from re-enabling sale.

requirements.statement: Support an approximate remaining-use allowance for a shared critical ingredient or option, applying reservation, commitment, release, and manual correction without gram-level recipe inventory.
requirements.rationale: Items such as vegan mozzarella and gluten-free dough limit several configurations at once and need a lightweight ceiling; this is an explicit MVP decision.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-RECIPE-INVENTORY. How approximate uses are estimated is confirmed under JV-STOCK.

requirements.statement: Disable only the products and configurations that require an exhausted shared critical ingredient.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: blanket product shutdown on shared-ingredient depletion causes unnecessary lost sales.

requirements.statement: Allow an individual modifier option to be disabled while the product remains orderable in a valid configuration.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery requires removing only the unavailable option when a valid product configuration remains.

requirements.statement: Support an optional daily limit for a product using the same reserve, commit, and release semantics as unit stock.
requirements.rationale: Selected pizzas depend on limited preparations and need a per-day ceiling distinct from countable stock.
requirements.notes: Which pizzas require daily limits is confirmed under JV-STOCK.

requirements.statement: Support pickup-window-specific availability for selected limited products or options.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery permits limited items to be offered only in some pickup windows.

requirements.statement: Support a per-product service-day stock policy of carrying remaining stock over, requiring a fresh opening count, or requiring a closing outcome for retained, discarded, or corrected quantities.
requirements.rationale: Perishable and non-perishable countable products behave differently between service days; a single policy would misstate available stock at opening.
requirements.notes: Which products carry over and whether closing reconciliation is daily or product-specific is confirmed under JV-STOCK.

requirements.statement: Highlight repeated differences between expected and physical stock for responsible review.
requirements.rationale: Repeated discrepancies are the signal that stock records are unreliable, which is the precondition for later simplifying closing counts.

requirements.statement: Support a per-product low-stock threshold.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery states each countable product may define its own low-stock threshold, while leaving warning behaviour open.
requirements.notes: The exact warning behaviour remains explicitly open in canonical discovery and is not invented here.

requirements.statement: Allow Jaime or an authorised responsible person to create, edit, deactivate, reorder, reprice, feature, schedule, and hide products through a protected administration interface.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery requires Jaime to perform broad catalog administration without developer intervention.
requirements.notes: The capability is accepted. The approved initial catalog content is a separate concern governed by JV-CATALOG-APPROVAL.

requirements.statement: Restrict ingredient, allergen, dietary, price, commercial text, and other sensitive catalog changes to Jaime or an explicitly authorised responsible person, and deny them to temporary or reinforcement staff.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: unauthorised catalog changes alter safety information and produce incorrect dietary or allergen claims.

requirements.statement: Require reliable supplier or product documentation and an explicit responsible review before validating ingredients, allergens, or dietary rules.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: sensitive catalog data validated without evidence produces incorrect allergen or dietary information.

requirements.statement: Support product-specific allowed removals, substitutions, and paid extras through configured modifier groups and options rather than an unrestricted free-text ingredient editor.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery requires configured modifiers; free-text ingredient editing produces kitchen ambiguity and incorrect allergen results.
requirements.notes: The modifier mechanism is accepted; the per-pizza matrix and prices are calibrated under JV-MODIFIERS.

requirements.statement: Prevent a free-text kitchen note from overriding configured modifier eligibility, price, availability, or allergen rules.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: free-text notes bypassing configured modifiers create ambiguous or unsafe kitchen requests and invalidate the computed allergen result.
requirements.notes: Food-safety relevant: the allergen calculation is only trustworthy if notes cannot change the actual product.

requirements.statement: Restrict free-text notes to non-ingredient instructions and to exceptions explicitly authorised by Jaime.
requirements.rationale: Keeps the note channel bounded so it cannot become an unrestricted modification path.
requirements.notes: Which non-ingredient instructions are permitted is confirmed under JV-MODIFIERS.

requirements.statement: Do not reduce the displayed product price when an ingredient is removed, unless Jaime defines an explicit exception.
requirements.rationale: Records the current working pricing rule so implementation does not invent a discount behaviour.
requirements.notes: Whether removing ingredients always preserves price remains explicitly open under JV-MODIFIERS.

requirements.statement: Support an independent maximum quantity for each paid extra.
requirements.rationale: Prevents unbounded extras from breaking both pricing expectations and the production-point workload model.

requirements.statement: Prevent a product from participating in real orders until its bilingual name and required description, price, ingredients, regulated allergens, known traces, availability, and dietary labels are complete and approved.
requirements.rationale: Canonical closure lists complete validated product-specific allergen data as a blocker before the first real order; a general warning is explicitly insufficient.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from a public-launch to a pilot obligation per canonical section 18A. The prohibition on letting an incomplete product participate is accepted in sections 10.1A and 18A; only the approved catalog content and allergen matrix are outstanding. PILOT-004 carries the milestone block.

requirements.statement: Require a renewed ingredient, allergen, trace, and dietary review after any recipe, ingredient, quantity, or supplier change, and keep the affected product or option unavailable online until that review is complete.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: product or supplier changes bypassing allergen review leave outdated safety information online.
requirements.notes: Food-safety relevant. The unavailability is automatic, not discretionary.

requirements.statement: Permit publishing a price-only change without repeating the full allergen review only when recipe, quantity, product, and supplier are unchanged.
requirements.rationale: Bounds the exception to BR-CATALOG-003 so routine repricing is not blocked while genuine composition changes still trigger review.

requirements.statement: Allow any staff member who detects incorrect safety or dietary information to disable the affected product or option immediately and require notification of the responsible person.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: detection must be able to stop sales instantly, without waiting for an authorisation step.

requirements.statement: Support reviewed Spanish and Catalan product names and required descriptions, using the browser language on first visit where supported, a visible language selector, and Spanish as fallback.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an incomplete or unreviewed launch language gives customers inconsistent or misleading content.
requirements.notes: The bilingual mechanism, browser-language default, selector, and Spanish fallback are accepted in sections 10.1B and 3.1; only the final approved copy is outstanding. BR-LAUNCH-001 carries the public-launch block.

requirements.statement: Do not publish an automatic translation without human review.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an unreviewed automatic translation can misstate product or allergen information.
requirements.notes: Food-safety relevant through mistranslated ingredient and allergen text.

requirements.statement: Require a short composition description for pizzas, while permitting clearly named packaged drinks and desserts to omit a separate description.
requirements.rationale: Sets the minimum content bar for publication without imposing needless copy work on packaged items.

requirements.statement: Order products within a category with active featured products first, followed by Jaime's manual order.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery gives Jaime manual control of product order with featured products promoted within the category.

requirements.statement: Enforce temporary-product start and end dates and single-service hiding at add-to-cart and at final confirmation.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a temporary or service-hidden product that remains orderable sells a commercial offer Dopis is not making.

requirements.statement: Apply stock, availability, allergen, and publication validation before featured or recommended products are ranked or displayed.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: commercial presentation must not override operational and safety rules.

requirements.statement: Render a product without a photograph without reserving an empty visual area.
requirements.rationale: Photographs are optional, so the menu must remain presentable without them.

requirements.statement: Preserve the commercial description and confirmed price of historical and accepted orders despite later catalog changes or deactivation.
requirements.rationale: Removing a product from the active menu must not corrupt old orders or rewrite what a customer agreed to pay.

requirements.statement: Retain ingredients, regulated allergens, known traces, dietary labels, and cross-contact notices for each sellable configuration.
requirements.rationale: Complete product-specific allergen data is a canonical pilot blocker and the basis of every customer-facing allergen obligation.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 10.3 states that the catalog must store these fields, so the retention obligation is accepted; only the matrix content is outstanding. PILOT-004 carries the milestone block.

requirements.statement: Recalculate and display allergens for the final selected configuration and repeat them in the order summary before confirmation.
requirements.rationale: A customer configures a product before ordering, so allergens shown for the base product alone would be misleading at the point of decision.
requirements.notes: Food-safety relevant. The display obligation is accepted; only the underlying matrix content is gated.

requirements.statement: Warn the customer at selection time when a chosen modifier or substitution introduces an allergen.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: a customer choosing a substitution must learn about a newly introduced allergen at the moment of choice, not only in the final summary.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline. Canonical section 10.3 states it as a customer-facing requirement.

requirements.statement: Update the vegan and vegetarian classification of a product when a modifier changes its final composition.
requirements.rationale: Food safety and consumer accuracy: a stale dietary label on a modified product is a false claim.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Provide Vegan, Vegetarian, and Gluten-free dough option menu filters.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery lists these as the initial customer-facing dietary filters.
requirements.notes: The filter name deliberately says dough option rather than gluten-free, consistent with BR-ALLERGEN-001.

requirements.statement: Show clearly when an unavailable option changes the dietary configuration that can still be ordered.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: a customer relying on a dietary configuration must not silently receive a different one because an option ran out.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Present the option as a gluten-free dough option and do not claim suitability for coeliac customers or severe allergies.
requirements.rationale: Verified operating facts show gluten-free dough shares oven, workspace, and utensils, so a gluten-free claim for the finished pizza would be false and dangerous.
requirements.notes: Food-safety critical. Canonical section 10.3 already accepts the obligation not to claim coeliac or severe-allergy suitability; only the exact customer-facing wording is outstanding under JV-GLUTEN. The unresolved gate still blocks the PILOT milestone through PILOT-004.

requirements.statement: Show a general cross-contact warning in the menu.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: the shared oven and utensils create a real cross-contact risk that must be communicated before product selection.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 10.3 states the general menu cross-contact warning as an interface obligation. Only its exact wording is outstanding under JV-GLUTEN.

requirements.statement: Show a specific cross-contact warning when the customer selects the gluten-free dough option.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: canonical discovery requires a specific warning at the point of selection in addition to the general menu warning.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 10.3 states the selection-time warning as an interface obligation. Only its exact wording is outstanding under JV-GLUTEN.

requirements.statement: Require explicit customer confirmation that the cross-contact warning has been read and understood before a gluten-free dough configuration can be ordered.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: canonical section 10.3 requires explicit confirmation that the customer has read and understood the cross-contact warning, which is the strongest customer-facing control available before the validated kitchen procedure exists.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 10.3 already imposes the explicit acknowledgement obligation, so it is accepted here. Only the exact acknowledgement wording is outstanding under JV-GLUTEN.

requirements.statement: State that online ordering cannot guarantee the absence of cross-contact and advise customers with severe allergies to contact the premises before ordering.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: online ordering removes the conversation in which a severe allergy would normally be raised, so the limitation must be stated.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 10.3 states both the no-guarantee statement and the severe-allergy contact advice as interface obligations. Only their exact wording is outstanding under JV-GLUTEN.

requirements.statement: Allow authorised staff to disable the gluten-free dough option independently of the products that offer it.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: the option must be stoppable without withdrawing every pizza, otherwise staff face a choice between closing the menu and selling an unsafe option.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 10.3 states independent disablement as an interface obligation. Linked to JV-GLUTEN for consistency with OPS-GLUTEN-001, which governs when the disablement must be exercised.

requirements.statement: Disable the gluten-free dough option whenever the validated operating procedure cannot be followed.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: the option is only as safe as the kitchen procedure behind it, so it must stop when that procedure lapses.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 10.3 states the disablement obligation itself. Only the detailed conditions under which the validated procedure counts as unfollowable are outstanding under JV-GLUTEN.

requirements.statement: On discovering that published allergen information is incorrect, immediately disable the affected product or option for new sales and pause the affected service scope until the discrepancy is resolved.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: containment must stop new exposure before any review work begins.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous combined requirement so containment and accepted-order review are verified separately. The pause obligation was missing from the previous statement.

requirements.statement: On discovering that published allergen information is incorrect, identify accepted orders not yet handed over that include the affected configuration, route them to operational review, and preserve the incident and correction trail.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: customers holding an already accepted order are the population at actual risk and must be identified explicitly.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous combined requirement.

requirements.statement: Support authorised substitutions defined either as a specific product relationship or as a validated category and price fallback rule, applying the specific relationship in preference to the fallback.
requirements.rationale: Canonical closure lists approved substitution rules as a pilot blocker; without them staff have no sanctioned way to resolve an unavailable accepted item.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 6.19 defines the two-tier substitution mechanism and section 7.9 states the preference order, so the obligation is accepted; the concrete relationships and fallback rules are content set by Jaime. OPS-STOCK-001 depends on this requirement rather than the reverse.

requirements.statement: Prevent the delegated responsible person from applying a substitution outside the approved relationships and fallback rules.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an improvised substitution creates safety, pricing, and customer-dispute exposure.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 7.9 states that the delegated responsible person may not improvise outside approved rules, so the prohibition is accepted; only the approved rule set is outstanding.

requirements.statement: Record the customer's substitution choice and leave the original product's published price unchanged.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: uncontrolled substitution changing published pricing causes customer disputes and catalog inconsistency.

requirements.statement: Limit a price difference absorbed as an incident resolution to the fixed per-order maximum configured by Jaime, and collect or escalate any larger difference.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: unbounded absorbed price differences produce inconsistent financial decisions.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 7.9 accepts collecting or absorbing a price difference within Jaime's configured per-order limit, so the obligation is accepted and the maximum is a value. Section 18A lists the approved limit as a pilot blocker, which PILOT-004 carries.

requirements.statement: Record reason, operational loss, actor, and timestamp when an already prepared order is cancelled.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: prepared-order cancellation without loss recording leaves operational waste and responsibility unclear.
requirements.notes: Operational loss is recorded as an occurrence without calculating a monetary amount in the first MVP.

requirements.statement: Present only manually configured recommendations whose recommended product is published, active, available, allergen-complete, temporally valid, and compatible with the customer's selected dietary configuration.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an unavailable or dietary-incompatible recommendation is misleading and potentially unsafe.
requirements.notes: The eligibility rules are accepted; the concrete pilot relationships are approved under JV-CATALOG-APPROVAL.

requirements.statement: Display the same allergen and dietary information on a recommendation as in the product's normal menu presentation.
requirements.rationale: Food safety: a recommendation is an ordering surface and must not present less safety information than the menu.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Allow upselling to be disabled globally or for an individual source product without removing recommended products from the menu.
requirements.rationale: Gives Jaime a way to stop recommendations during the pilot without damaging the catalog.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Keep upselling optional and non-blocking, limited to at most three recommendations across the whole cart, with no automatic item addition and no automatic quantity increase.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: upselling that reduces checkout completion harms the primary MVP goal.
requirements.notes: Enforces part of EXC-RECOMMENDATION-ENGINE.

requirements.statement: Exclude from recommendation any product already in the cart and any recommendation the customer has already ignored during the current checkout.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: repeatedly showing an ignored recommendation makes checkout intrusive.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Merge configured relationships across every pizza in the cart, remove duplicates, and apply the configured priority order.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a multi-pizza cart otherwise produces duplicate and excessive prompts.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Revalidate publication, stock, availability, capacity, allergen data, and dietary compatibility when a recommendation is added, using the ordinary add-to-cart path.
requirements.rationale: Prevents the recommendation surface from becoming a route that bypasses the normal ordering checks.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Warn the customer and require an explicit keep-or-remove decision when a later pizza modification makes an already-added recommendation incompatible, and never remove a cart item silently.
requirements.rationale: Food safety and consumer accuracy: silent removal or a silently incompatible item both mislead the customer about what they are buying.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Record aggregate recommendation impressions and additions by placement, without constructing persistent individual recommendation profiles.
requirements.rationale: Pilot evidence is needed to decide whether upselling is retained, while canonical privacy rules forbid individual profiling.
requirements.notes: Placements are post-pizza and cart review.

requirements.statement: After order submission, send one SMS providing secure access to private order tracking.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery requires guest customers to receive one SMS containing secure access to tracking after submission.
requirements.notes: Exact wording and retry behaviour remain open under JV-DELAYS; the obligation to send the access SMS is confirmed.

requirements.statement: Send an SMS when an order becomes ready, or is rejected or cancelled by staff.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery lists these three outcomes as the required additional SMS notifications.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous combined requirement so the positive notification duty and the no-acceptance-SMS rule verify separately.

requirements.statement: Do not send an acceptance SMS; show acceptance on the web and private tracking page instead.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery explicitly rejects a redundant acceptance SMS, which would add cost and message fatigue without operational value.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous combined FR-COMMS-002.

requirements.statement: Show every material pickup-estimate revision on the private tracking page.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery requires every material revision to appear in tracking, independently of whether an SMS is also sent.
requirements.notes: What counts as a material revision is deliberately deferred to JV-DELAYS rather than invented here.

requirements.statement: Leave the decision to send an additional SMS for a further material estimate revision to staff, and update tracking without requiring another SMS for an agreed pickup extension.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery leaves repeated-revision messaging to staff judgement and exempts an agreed extension from a further SMS.
requirements.notes: Whether repeated estimate changes require additional SMS messages remains open under JV-DELAYS.

requirements.statement: Require an opaque, high-entropy, time-limited, single-use access token exchanged for a protected browser session for private tracking; a sequential public order code shall never authorise access.
requirements.rationale: Guest tracking exposes personal order data without an account, so access control is the only barrier protecting it.
requirements.notes: The token mechanism is retained as a requirement because canonical discovery states it as a confirmed security model, not as a design preference.

requirements.statement: Keep the tracking page read-only for the order lifecycle except for accepting or declining a proposed alternative pickup time and rejecting an important revised estimate, granting no general order editing or self-service cancellation.
requirements.rationale: Bounds the only customer-writable surface so it cannot become the deferred self-service cancellation capability.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-SELF-CANCEL. Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Allow a tracking session to be revoked and expire it after a configurable retention period.
requirements.rationale: An indefinitely valid tracking session keeps personal order data reachable long after the order is complete.
requirements.notes: The retention period depends on the approved retention rules and is calibrated under JV-PRIVACY.

requirements.statement: Limit SMS content to Dopis identification, general order status, and the private tracking link, excluding complete order detail.
requirements.rationale: SMS is an unprotected channel that may be read on a lock screen or by a shared device.

requirements.statement: Take payment at the premises and do not offer online card payment, Apple Pay, or Google Pay.
requirements.rationale: Preserves the explicit first-MVP exclusion of online payment while keeping the order domain extensible for it later.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-PAYMENT-ONLINE.

requirements.statement: Allow staff to record the payment method actually used at collection as cash or card, without the customer preselecting it during ordering.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery records that cash discrepancies frequently come from card payments recorded as cash, so the recorded method must reflect what actually happened.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked. The obligation is accepted in sections 3.2, 6.6, and 7.5; only receipt and correction procedure detail remains open.

requirements.statement: Keep payment and handover as separate recorded events and prevent handover until an accepted payment method has succeeded.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: collapsing payment and handover into one action allows unpaid orders to be released and makes the audit trail unclear.
requirements.notes: Whether any exceptional unpaid handover is permitted remains open under JV-PAYMENT-PROCEDURE.

requirements.statement: Allow a failed card payment to be retried or changed to cash, and record an operational incident with no handover when no accepted method succeeds.
requirements.rationale: Defines the failure path so staff are not left improvising at the counter with a prepared order.

requirements.statement: Preserve prior events, actor, timestamp, and a required reason for every correction to payment method, paid state, or handover state.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: payment or handover corrected without traceability makes cash and order history unreliable.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked; the append-only correction trail is accepted in section 6.6.

requirements.statement: Restrict reversal of a mistakenly paid state to Jaime or the responsible shift lead and require a reason.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery reserves paid-state reversal to responsible staff because it directly affects cash reconciliation.

requirements.statement: Allow an order marked handed over in error to return to READY while preserving the original handover event.
requirements.rationale: Provides the defined correction path for a mistaken handover instead of deleting or rewriting the event.
requirements.notes: How an erroneous handover is corrected in practice remains open under JV-PAYMENT-PROCEDURE.

requirements.statement: At shift close, compare expected and actual cash and allow an explanation to be recorded for any difference.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a cash discrepancy not reviewed at shift close leaves repeated accounting errors unexplained.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous combined shift-close requirement; the responsible-confirmation duty is now OPS-SHIFT-001.

requirements.statement: Require the responsible person to review open orders, payments, and unresolved incidents and to confirm shift close explicitly; incidents shall not close automatically.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an incident hidden to permit shift close loses a material unresolved decision.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous combined AUDIT-PAYMENT-002.

requirements.statement: Close responsible operational sessions at shift end.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: staff sessions remaining active after a shift permit unauthorised later access.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline. Session lifetime is confirmed under JV-ACCESS.

requirements.statement: Provide a visible Requires attention queue for orders, failures, and customer responses needing staff action.
requirements.rationale: Multiple exception paths route work to staff attention; without a single visible destination those routings are unobservable.

requirements.statement: Support staff contact and resolution of non-collection, invalid contact, delay, shortage, and payment incidents.
requirements.rationale: Canonical sections 7.5 and 3.2 accept staff-led incident contact and resolution as the operating model; without it the exception queue has no resolution path.
requirements.notes: Split so the accepted resolution obligation is no longer held back by the provisional repeat-incident rule. The prohibition on automatic customer blocking is BR-INCIDENT-003; the provisional two-incidents-in-90-days rule is BR-INCIDENT-002.

requirements.statement: Do not automatically block or refuse a customer on the basis of recorded operational incidents.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery states that incident handling must not automatically block a customer; an automatic block would penalise real customers on an unvalidated fairness rule.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous combined statement so the accepted prohibition is verified independently of the provisional repeat-incident rule in BR-INCIDENT-002.

requirements.statement: Route a customer with two or more operational incidents within 90 days to manual review.
requirements.rationale: Canonical section 3.2 records the rule as a provisional working direction; it is stated here so it is visible and governed rather than implicit, without being accepted.
requirements.notes: Recorded as a candidate obligation only. Canonical section 3.2 marks the rule as explicitly pending fairness and privacy validation, and section 11.5 states that the 90-day window is not a retention policy. It must not be implemented before JV-INCIDENT-FAIRNESS resolves.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: whether the provisional two-incidents-in-90-days rule is operationally appropriate
block_justifications.explanation: Canonical section 3.2 marks the rule itself as pending fairness and privacy validation. What is undecided is whether Dopis applies the rule at all, not how it is worded or operated.

requirements.statement: Record a delay attributable to Dopis as a local operational incident that does not affect the customer's incident history.
requirements.rationale: Fairness: a customer must not accumulate a negative record because Dopis missed its own commitment.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Keep incidents, corrections, reopenings, and interim operational measures traceable without deleting prior history.
requirements.rationale: Append-only history is what makes an accidental correction reconstructable rather than silently overwritten.

requirements.statement: Allow Jaime or an authorised responsible person to reopen an incorrectly resolved incident, preserving the original record and linking the continuation.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an incorrect incident resolution that cannot be revisited becomes a permanent operational or customer-history error.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Retain actor and timestamp for availability and stock changes, and additionally retain previous and new values for price, text, and sensitive-configuration changes.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: sensitive catalog edits overwriting prior values make incorrect content impossible to reconstruct.
requirements.notes: Routine commercial changes do not require a written reason; exceptional corrections do.

requirements.statement: When a problem exceeds authorised rules, allow staff to pause only the affected product, option, channel, or capability while unaffected operation remains safe.
requirements.rationale: Safe isolation keeps the rest of the service running, but which measures count as safe is an unresolved stakeholder decision.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 7.9 states scoped pausing and the lowest-risk measure as the accepted response, so the obligation is accepted; which measures count as operationally safe is outstanding.

requirements.statement: Retain a pending-Jaime decision record holding the related order or incident, the safe operational measure applied, a summary of the unresolved decision, the responsible shift lead, the creation time, the review status, and Jaime's resolution.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: an incident hidden to permit shift close loses a material unresolved decision; the record is what makes safe close possible.
requirements.notes: Omitted entirely from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Allow a shift to close with an open pending-Jaime decision only when immediate operation is safe and the item remains visibly tracked.
requirements.rationale: Bounds the safe-close exception so it cannot become a way to dispose of unresolved decisions.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 7.9 states the shift-close condition verbatim, so the obligation is accepted; it depends on the same safe-measure definition as OPS-INCIDENT-001.

requirements.statement: Present open pending-Jaime decisions at the next service opening and in Jaime's next review report.
requirements.rationale: A pending decision that is recorded but never surfaced is equivalent to a lost decision.
requirements.notes: How and when Jaime receives the pending-decision summary remains open under JV-SHIFT-AUTHORITY.

requirements.statement: Maintain one bounded operational threshold register recording, for every outstanding operating value, the concept, initial value, pilot adjustability, review moment, and validator.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: discovery continuing through repetitive numeric interviews. The register is the canonical mechanism consolidating every unresolved number, and every CALIBRATE link in this baseline resolves through it.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 6.20 accepts the register and its columns, so the obligation to maintain it is accepted; the rows are the content JV-THRESHOLDS supplies. Section 18A lists loaded threshold values as a pilot blocker, which PILOT-004 carries.

requirements.statement: Keep operational threshold values configurable rather than fixed in code, and load conservative initial values before the pilot.
requirements.rationale: Canonical closure permits values to remain provisional at pilot start only if they can be adjusted from evidence without redeployment.

requirements.statement: Prevent online ordering from opening until Jaime or a currently authorised delegate assumes and records responsibility for the service.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a service running without accountable responsibility. Opening is blocked when neither authorised person is present.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked: the pilot may begin with Jaime as the only responsible person, so the opening rule is implementable now. Only the nominal delegate identity is pending, which is a WITHOUT_JAIME concern.

requirements.statement: Represent principal and delegated responsibility explicitly, including whether delegated authority is stable or limited to specified shifts or dates.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: delegated authority expired or absent at opening. Delegation must never be inferred from seniority or mere presence.
requirements.notes: Canonical sections 6.5 and 11.7 accept explicit representation of principal and delegated responsibility, so the obligation is accepted; the nominal delegate and the authorisation dates are content. OPS-DELEGATION-001 carries the operating-without-Jaime block.

requirements.statement: Do not operate a service without Jaime present until the nominal delegated responsible person is confirmed, the authorisation dates or conditions are recorded, evidence exists that the delegate understands the approved rules, limits, and safe measures, and bounded access is active.
requirements.rationale: Canonical section 18A states four operating-without-Jaime blockers that no baseline record carried. Without this record, unblocking the individual delegation obligations would leave the milestone condition itself unrepresented.
requirements.notes: Added during the Owner-review correction pass. This is the WITHOUT_JAIME analogue of PILOT-004: it is where unresolved delegation and access gates block the milestone, so the obligations it depends on can be baselined.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: dates or conditions of delegated authorisation before operating without Jaime
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A operating-without-Jaime blockers that the nominal delegate is confirmed, the authorisation dates or conditions are recorded, and the delegate understands the approved rules, limits, and safe measures. Until Jaime confers that authorisation, entry to the milestone is not permitted.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: what exact onboarding, revocation, and access-review procedure will Jaime use
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A operating-without-Jaime blocker that access is active and bounded. Bounded access cannot be conferred before the onboarding, revocation, and access-review procedure exists.

requirements.statement: Reserve authorisation, revocation, and permission changes for staff access to Jaime.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a shift lead able to change access permissions produces privilege expansion without owner control.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked. The Jaime-only rule is confirmed in sections 3.2, 6.5, and 11.7; only the procedure is open.

requirements.statement: Limit temporary staff and shared kitchen sessions to operational access without sensitive administration capability.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: shared kitchen access exposing administration lets temporary staff change sensitive data.

requirements.statement: Remove departing-staff access before the next service and support a Jaime review of active access before the pilot and whenever personnel change.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: departing staff retaining access permits unauthorised access after employment.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Keep personal and administrative credentials individual and never shared.
requirements.rationale: The shared kitchen session is an explicitly bounded exception; extending sharing to personal or administrative credentials would destroy attribution entirely.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Record the responsible person at opening, at responsibility handover with its time, during shared-session use, and at shift close, without claiming individual attribution for shared-session actions.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: shared access mistaken for individual attribution produces a misleading audit history.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked: honest attribution is implementable now and does not depend on naming the delegate.

requirements.statement: Require confirmation of the customer name or order identifier in addition to a telephone lookup before disclosing order information by telephone.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a caller identified only by telephone number may receive another person's order information.

requirements.statement: Limit routine telephone support disclosure to order status and estimated pickup time.
requirements.rationale: Verifying the caller is necessary but not sufficient; the amount disclosed must also be bounded.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline, which covered verification but not the disclosure limit.

requirements.statement: Show previous incidents as a minimal summary in operational views, with detail available only when operationally necessary.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: incident summaries exposing excessive history give staff more personal context than they need.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Restrict weekly reports and export of order, telephone, commercial, or operational data to Jaime or explicitly authorised people.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: broadly exportable reports or telephone lists remove commercial and personal data from controlled use.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked; the restriction is confirmed in sections 3.2, 11.7, and 12.3.

requirements.statement: Record report access and data exports.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk mitigation explicitly includes auditing exports; a restriction that is never observed cannot be shown to hold.
requirements.notes: Canonical wording is auditable where proportionate, so this is SHOULD rather than MUST.

requirements.statement: Before collecting name and telephone number, explain that the data are used to manage and fulfil the order, communicate status changes or operational incidents, and locate the order when the customer contacts Dopis.
requirements.rationale: Canonical closure requires a minimum viable privacy notice to be active from the first real pilot order, not only at public launch.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked by a public-launch gate. Blocking this would have deferred a control that sections 11.4, 12.4, and 18A require from the first real order.

requirements.statement: Do not treat operational contact data as a customer account, commercial profile, loyalty enrolment, or marketing consent.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: operational telephone data reused for marketing creates invalid consent and loss of trust.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-ACCOUNTS-LOYALTY.

requirements.statement: Keep any commercial consent separate from checkout, optional, explicit, unchecked by default, and revocable.
requirements.rationale: Stated as a negative constraint on the MVP checkout so no consent control can be added to it silently.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline. The first MVP collects no commercial consent at all; this bounds any future addition.

requirements.statement: Keep telephone numbers hidden in routine operational queues on both the tablet and the mobile backup, revealing them only through an explicit Contact customer action.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: telephone numbers visible throughout kitchen operations cause unnecessary personal-data exposure.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked; least-necessary visibility is an accepted rule and a minimum pilot control.

requirements.statement: Route personal-data access, correction, and deletion requests to Jaime through a documented procedure rather than to kitchen staff during active service.
