requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: data requests handled informally during service cause incorrect disclosure, deletion, or missed requests. Canonical section 11.4 requires a minimum viable form from the first real pilot order.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked. The full procedure and identity checks are defined before public launch, but a minimum viable routing must exist for the pilot.

requirements.statement: Apply the retention and anonymisation periods approved through the compliance review to identified orders, telephone numbers, incidents, payment and cash-close records, audit events, and SMS delivery records.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: retention periods undefined at public launch leave personal data retained indefinitely.
requirements.notes: The obligation to apply the periods approved through the compliance review is accepted and stateable; the periods themselves are values that must not be invented, and the anonymisation approach is procedure. The provisional 90-day incident window is explicitly not a retention policy. BR-LAUNCH-001 carries the public-launch block.

requirements.statement: Do not open the service to public launch until the applicable compliance review is complete, retention periods are defined, the personal-data request procedure is defined, public customer and privacy texts are approved, relevant processors are reviewed, applicable cookie, electronic-contracting, and consumer obligations are addressed, and production security and operational readiness are validated.
requirements.rationale: Canonical section 18A states seven public-launch blockers that no baseline record carried. Without this record, unblocking the individual retention and content obligations would leave the milestone condition itself unrepresented.
requirements.notes: Added during the Owner-review correction pass. This is the PUBLIC_LAUNCH analogue of PILOT-004: it is where unresolved compliance, privacy, and content gates block the milestone, so the obligations it depends on can be baselined.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: how long should identified orders, telephone numbers, incidents, payment records, and audit events be retained
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A public-launch blockers that the applicable compliance review is complete, retention periods are defined, and the applicable cookie, electronic-contracting, and consumer obligations are addressed.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: what exact procedure and identity checks will Jaime use for access, correction, or deletion requests
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A public-launch blockers that the personal-data request procedure is defined and the relevant processors are reviewed.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: final Spanish and Catalan names and descriptions
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A public-launch blocker that the public customer and privacy texts are approved.

requirements.statement: Do not store payment-card data.
requirements.rationale: Canonical privacy technical baseline requires avoiding direct storage of payment-card data; with pay-at-premises there is no legitimate reason to hold it.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Use anonymised or aggregated data for metrics wherever identifiable records are no longer required.
requirements.rationale: Reduces the identifiable data surface of routine reporting without waiting for final retention periods.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Apply the privacy notice, minimum access controls, security measures, and personal-data request procedure from the first real pilot order.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: pilot status used to defer privacy controls means real customer data is handled without safeguards.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline. This is the requirement that makes the pilot-milestone privacy reclassifications binding.

requirements.statement: Before pilot activation, record two complete weeks of order counts by WEB, PHONE, and IN_PERSON, by time band, together with calls used to create and to modify an order.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a pilot starting without a reliable baseline makes call-reduction claims unevaluable.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 12.2 accepts the two-week pre-pilot baseline and its dimensions; the exact days, time bands, and observer ownership are values and ownership set under JV-PILOT.

requirements.statement: Do not set a numeric call-reduction target before the real baseline exists.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery explicitly forbids inventing the target in advance; a fabricated target would misdirect the whole pilot evaluation.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Run the first real pilot segment as an approximately one-hour session with a limited group of informed regular customers on a lower-pressure Wednesday or Thursday.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a pilot expanding too quickly makes peak-service failures harder to isolate.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 12.4 accepts the first-segment shape; the participant group and exact date are content set under JV-PILOT. PILOT-004 carries the milestone block.

requirements.statement: Before the first real pilot order, run and pass a complete operational rehearsal covering web, telephone, and in-person orders, alerts and acknowledgement, delays and revised estimates, sold-out products and stock conflicts, connection loss and recovery, payment and handover, and shift close.
requirements.rationale: The rehearsal is the canonical evidence that the whole operating flow works before real customers are exposed to it.
requirements.notes: Canonical sections 12.4 and 18A accept the rehearsal and its coverage; only the exact pass evidence is outstanding under JV-PILOT. PILOT-004 carries the milestone block.

requirements.statement: Keep all web orders in manual review at pilot start, and enable automatic acceptance only after operating hours, capacity, alerts and acknowledgement, stock and availability, order reception, and order handling have been demonstrated reliable.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: automatic acceptance enabled before operations are proven lets orders bypass unresolved capacity, stock, or alert failures.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline. The promotion criteria are calibrated, but the manual-review default is accepted now.

requirements.statement: Require explicit validated criteria before transitioning to automatic acceptance, rolling back from it, or expanding to the full service schedule.
requirements.rationale: Canonical discovery states these three transitions require explicit validated criteria that do not yet exist.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 12.5 accepts the requirement for explicit validated criteria; the criteria themselves are content set under JV-PILOT.

requirements.statement: Do not begin the pilot until the participating catalog is approved, product-specific ingredients and allergens are validated, hours, stock, and availability are confirmed, alerts and order reception are verified, conservative thresholds are loaded, substitution rules and the absorbed-price limit are approved, simulated and real data are separated, minimum privacy, access, security, and rights-request controls are active, and Jaime or an authorised responsible person is present.
requirements.rationale: Restates the canonical pilot-entry blockers as a single gate so no individual precondition can be waived silently.
requirements.notes: Substitution rules, the absorbed-price limit, and the gluten gate were missing from the previous statement despite appearing in the canonical section 18A blocker list. This record is where an unresolved pilot gate blocks the PILOT milestone globally, which is why the individual obligations it depends on can be baselined.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: exact pass evidence from the operational rehearsal
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A pilot blockers that the operational rehearsal passes and that alerts and order reception are verified. Authorisation to begin the pilot cannot be conferred before that evidence exists.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: the complete allergen matrix for products and modifiers
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A pilot blocker that product-specific ingredients and allergens are complete and validated before the first real order.
Carries the canonical section 18A pilot blocker that the initial participating catalog is approved.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: which ingredients and options belong to the critical opening checklist
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A pilot blocker that initial hours, stock, and availability are confirmed, including the critical opening checklist the pre-opening gate reviews.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: the initial large-order manual-review threshold percentage
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A pilot blocker that conservative threshold values are loaded before the first real order.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: the fixed per-order amount the delegate may absorb
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the canonical section 18A pilot blocker that substitution rules and the absorbed-price limit are approved.

block_justifications.canonical_open_question: which severe-allergy requests the premises can responsibly accept
block_justifications.explanation: Carries the pilot offer policy for the gluten-free dough option. The individual section 10.3 gluten obligations are accepted and baselined; what is not conferred is authorisation to offer the option in a real pilot service before Jaime validates supplier documentation, the kitchen procedure, and the severe-allergy policy.

requirements.statement: Pause the affected pilot scope for a missing accepted order, an accepted order that is materially too late for reasonable fulfilment, repeatedly unattended alerts, or incorrect allergen information.
requirements.rationale: These are the canonical critical failures; continuing to serve customers through them is the outcome the pilot exists to prevent.
requirements.notes: An isolated manageable delay does not by itself require a pause. What counts as materially too late is calibrated under JV-DELAYS.

requirements.statement: On recurrence of a critical failure after it was considered corrected, return to manual review or pause the affected capability and investigate the cause before resuming, rather than only recording it in the weekly report.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: a reappearing critical fault that is only reported allows known unsafe or unreliable behaviour to continue.
requirements.notes: Split from the previous PILOT-005, which combined the pause trigger and the recurrence rule.

requirements.statement: Exclude simulated and internal-test orders from real pilot calculations, or report them in a separately labelled test-data segment.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: test orders contaminating pilot metrics make adoption and reliability results misleading.

requirements.statement: Evaluate the pilot after four complete weeks against reliability, adoption, operational value, on-time performance, commercial observation, and controlled progression.
requirements.rationale: The four-week scorecard is the canonical decision point for whether the system continues and what capability follows.
requirements.notes: Canonical section 12.3 accepts the four-week evaluation and its dimensions; the adoption and call-reduction thresholds are values pending the real baseline.

requirements.statement: Ensure no accepted order is lost or reaches the kitchen materially too late for reasonable fulfilment.
requirements.rationale: This is the canonical primary reliability criterion and the single condition on which the pilot is judged to have failed.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked: the obligation is accepted and already drives design; only the materially-too-late threshold is calibratable.

requirements.statement: Measure opening time, closing time, and correction count during the pilot before fixing a permanent acceptable operational workload limit.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: opening and closing workload assumed rather than measured may make the system unsustainable for a two-person operation.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Provide Jaime with a weekly report covering orders by channel, peak periods, incidents, delays, on-time performance, channel-specific average order value, best-selling products, and frequent product combinations.
requirements.rationale: Confirmed discovery specifies the weekly summary content; it is the evidence channel for the four-week evaluation.
requirements.notes: Reclassified from blocked: the report content is confirmed in sections 3.2 and 12.3.

requirements.statement: Measure on-time performance as delayed-order count, percentage prepared within the promised pickup window, and average delay.
requirements.rationale: Defines the on-time dimension of the scorecard concretely so it can be computed rather than judged.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Record manual capacity override usage.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk mitigation requires measuring override usage so it does not quietly become routine.
requirements.notes: Omitted from the previous baseline.

requirements.statement: Do not provide coupon codes, discount codes, automatic compensation rules, future credits, or loyalty benefits; permit staff only to record the resolution actually agreed with the customer inside the incident.
requirements.rationale: Named canonical risk: compensation implemented before business approval causes scope expansion and inconsistent commercial treatment.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-COMPENSATION. Omitted from the previous baseline, whose exclusion list did not mention compensation at all.

requirements.statement: Offer one pizza size and do not offer half-and-half pizzas.
requirements.rationale: Preserves two explicit canonical product-scope exclusions that a modifier requirement could otherwise reintroduce.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-HALF-AND-HALF.

requirements.statement: Do not provide discounts, dynamic pricing, automatic promotions, recommendations inferred from sales, or random recommendations.
requirements.rationale: Preserves the explicit commercial-automation exclusions so upselling cannot drift into a recommendation engine.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-RECOMMENDATION-ENGINE.

requirements.statement: Do not depend on a ticket printer for normal operation; the digital panel remains the operational source of truth.
requirements.rationale: Preserves an explicit canonical exclusion and prevents a printer dependency from becoming an unstated operational prerequisite.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-PRINTER. A printer is reconsidered only after real operational testing.

requirements.statement: Do not offer coffee products.
requirements.rationale: Preserves an explicit canonical menu-scope exclusion.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-COFFEE.

requirements.statement: Limit bilingual content to public customer-facing material and do not provide a multilingual administration interface.
requirements.rationale: Preserves an explicit canonical exclusion that the bilingual content requirement could otherwise be read to extend.
requirements.notes: Enforces EXC-MULTILINGUAL-ADMIN.
